problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+4y \\ 5x+10y\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation

feedback.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y+z \\ -6x+3y-3z \\ 4x-2y+2z\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$
feedback.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}2\cdot 3-1+k \\ -6\cdot 3+3\cdot 1-3\cdot k \\ 4\cdot 3-2\cdot 1+2\cdot k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5+k \\ -15-3k \\ 10+2k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}5+k=0 \\ -15-3k=0 \\ 10+2k=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=-5.$
